name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q01 - Organization and divisions of human peripheral nervous system

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the organization of the human neural system:

Statement I: The central neural system (CNS) comprises the brain and the spinal cord and serves as the site of information processing and control.

Statement II: Afferent nerve fibres transmit sensory impulses from peripheral tissues and organs toward the central neural system.

Statement III: The somatic neural system transmits involuntary regulatory impulses from the central neural system to smooth muscles.

Statement IV: The visceral nervous system is a component of the peripheral nervous system comprising nerves, fibres, ganglia, and plexuses connecting the central neural system with the viscera.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human neural system is divided anatomically into the central neural system (CNS) and peripheral neural system (PNS). The PNS is further organized into functional divisions categorized by the direction of impulse conduction and the voluntary or involuntary nature of the target effectors.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding the central neural system
The central neural system consists of the brain and spinal cord, serving as the master integration center for information processing, command, and physiological control. Hence, this anatomical definition is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding afferent nerve fibres
Afferent nerve fibres conduct sensory impulses centripetally from sensory receptors, tissues, and peripheral organs inward to the central neural system. Hence, this directional role is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding the somatic neural system
The somatic neural system conducts voluntary impulses from the central neural system specifically to skeletal muscles, whereas conduction to smooth muscles and involuntary organs is performed by the autonomic neural system. Hence, attributing smooth muscle control to the somatic system is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding the visceral nervous system
The visceral nervous system represents the complex of nerves, fibres, ganglia, and plexuses of the peripheral neural system mediating reciprocal impulse traffic between the central neural system and the viscera. Hence, this anatomical characterization is factually accurate.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements concerning the central neural system, afferent nerve fibres, and visceral nervous system are correct, whereas the statement mischaracterizing the somatic neural system as controlling smooth muscles is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and IV are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.
Statements I, III, and IV are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q02 - Structural parts and classifications of human neurons

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the structure and types of neurons:

Statement I: Dendrites are short, repeatedly branching projections that conduct nerve impulses away from the cell body toward downstream synapses.

Statement II: Nissl's granules are granular cytoplasmic bodies found within the cell body and dendrites of a neuron.

Statement III: Multipolar neurons possess one axon and two or more dendrites and are characteristically located in the cerebral cortex.

Statement IV: Bipolar neurons possess one axon and one dendrite and are typically found in the retina of the eye.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
A neuron consists morphologically of a soma (cell body), receptive dendrites, and an impulse-transmitting axon, and is classified into distinct structural subtypes depending on the number of processes emerging from the cell body.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding dendrite conduction direction
Dendrites are receptive fibres that convey incoming electrical impulses centripetally toward the cell body, whereas the axon conducts impulses centrifugally away from the cell body. Hence, asserting that dendrites convey impulses away from the cell body is incorrect.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding Nissl's granules
Nissl's granules are granular assemblies of rough endoplasmic reticulum and ribosomes distributed in the cytoplasm of the soma and dendrites, while being absent from the axon. Hence, this cytological distribution is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding multipolar neurons
Multipolar neurons feature a single axon and two or more branching dendrites, constituting the dominant neuronal architecture within the cerebral cortex. Hence, this morphological classification is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding bipolar neurons
Bipolar neurons possess precisely two processes—one axon and one dendrite extending from opposite poles of the soma—and occur characteristically in sensory structures such as the retina of the eye. Hence, this anatomical location is factually accurate.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements describing Nissl's granules, multipolar neurons, and bipolar neurons are correct, whereas the statement misrepresenting dendrites as conducting impulses away from the cell body is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are correct, while Statement IV is incorrect.
Statements II, III, and IV are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I, III, and IV are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III, and IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q03 - Myelinated and unmyelinated nerve fibre characteristics

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding myelinated and unmyelinated nerve fibres:

Statement I: Schwann cells wrap around myelinated nerve fibres to form an insulating myelin sheath along the axon.

Statement II: The uninsulated gaps located between two adjacent myelin sheaths along an axon are termed nodes of Ranvier.

Statement III: Unmyelinated nerve fibres completely lack any covering or association with Schwann cells.

Statement IV: Myelinated nerve fibres are typically found in cranial and spinal nerves, whereas unmyelinated fibres are commonly found in autonomous and somatic neural systems.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Axonal fibres in the nervous system are categorized as myelinated or unmyelinated based on the ultrastructural relationship between axonal membranes and supporting glial Schwann cells.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding Schwann cells and myelin formation
In myelinated axons, Schwann cells envelop the axonal cylinder and wrap multiple concentric layers of plasma membrane to generate a lipid-rich insulating myelin sheath. Hence, this histological relationship is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding nodes of Ranvier
The periodic discontinuities or bare gaps occurring along the axon between consecutive myelin sheaths formed by adjacent Schwann cells are designated nodes of Ranvier. Hence, this structural definition is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding glial association in unmyelinated fibres
An unmyelinated nerve fibre is enclosed by a Schwann cell; however, the Schwann cell does not wrap concentrically to form a myelin sheath. Thus, unmyelinated fibres are not devoid of Schwann cells. Hence, claiming that unmyelinated fibres completely lack Schwann cells is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding tissue distributions of nerve fibres
Myelinated axons predominate in cranial and spinal nerves, while unmyelinated nerve fibres are typically encountered in autonomic and somatic peripheral neural systems. Hence, this anatomical distribution is factually accurate.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements detailing the formation of myelin sheaths, the identification of nodes of Ranvier, and the normal anatomical distribution of both fibre types are correct, while the statement asserting that unmyelinated fibres lack Schwann cells is incorrect.

Statements I, III, and IV are correct, while Statement II is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q04 - Electrochemical basis of resting axonal membrane potential

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the resting membrane potential of an axon:

Statement I: In a resting axonal membrane, permeability to potassium ions \(\left(\text{K}^{+}\right)\) is comparatively greater than permeability to sodium ions \(\left(\text{Na}^{+}\right)\).

Statement II: The resting axonal membrane is virtually impermeable to negatively charged proteins present within the axoplasm.

Statement III: As a result of selective permeabilities, the axoplasm contains a high concentration of \(\text{K}^{+}\) and negatively charged proteins and a low concentration of \(\text{Na}^{+}\).

Statement IV: The sodium-potassium pump actively transports 3 sodium ions \(\left(\text{Na}^{+}\right)\) outwards for every 2 potassium ions \(\left(\text{K}^{+}\right)\) into the cell.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The resting membrane potential reflects an unequal steady-state distribution of inorganic ions and impermeant organic anions across the axolemma, maintained by differential channel permeabilities and active primary ATP-driven transport.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding passive resting permeabilities
In an unexcited neuron, non-gated potassium leak channels confer substantially higher resting permeability to potassium ions compared to sodium ions, to which the membrane is nearly impermeable. Hence, this permeability comparison is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding axoplasmic protein permeability
Large organic anions, specifically intracellular proteins bearing negative net charges, are completely trapped within the axoplasm because the resting plasma membrane is impermeable to them. Hence, this membrane barrier property is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding steady-state intracellular concentrations
Due to selective leakage and active ion pumping, the intracellular axoplasmic fluid exhibits high potassium ion concentration, high impermeant protein concentration, and low sodium ion concentration relative to the extracellular fluid. Hence, this ionic profile is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding the sodium-potassium pump stoichiometry
The electrogenic sodium-potassium ATPase pump actively hydrolyzes ATP to extrude 3 sodium ions into the interstitial fluid while transporting 2 potassium ions into the axoplasm against their respective concentration gradients. Hence, this stoichiometry is factually accurate.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
All four evaluated assertions accurately describe the electrochemical, permeability, and active transport mechanisms underlying the resting membrane potential of the axon.

answer.text: Statements I and II are correct, but Statements III and IV are incorrect.
Statements I, II, and III are correct, while Statement IV is incorrect.
Statements II, III, and IV are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.
Statements I, II, III, and IV are all correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q05 - Electrophysiological mechanisms of nerve impulse generation propagation

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the generation and propagation of an action potential along an axon:

Statement I: Application of a stimulus causes a site on the axonal membrane to become freely permeable to \(\text{Na}^{+}\), leading to rapid \(\text{Na}^{+}\) influx.

Statement II: Rapid inward movement of \(\text{Na}^{+}\) reverses membrane polarity, making the inner surface positive and the outer surface negative.

Statement III: During action potential propagation, local current flows on the inner axonal surface from the adjacent resting site to the excited depolarized site.

Statement IV: The rise in stimulus-induced membrane permeability to \(\text{Na}^{+}\) is extremely short-lived and is rapidly succeeded by an increase in permeability to \(\text{K}^{+}\).

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The generation of an action potential involves transient voltage-dependent sodium influx causing depolarization and polarity reversal, which drives localized current loops that propagate the nerve impulse along the axonal length.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding initial sodium influx upon stimulation
When a threshold stimulus excites a resting site on the axonal membrane, voltage-gated sodium channels open rapidly, allowing sodium ions to rush down their electrochemical gradient into the axoplasm. Hence, this influx mechanism is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding polarity reversal during depolarization
The substantial entry of positive charge via incoming sodium ions reverses the electrical potential across the membrane, making the axoplasmic face electropositive relative to the electronegative external surface. Hence, this reversal of polarity is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding internal local current flow direction
At the excited locus, the interior is positive, whereas at the immediately adjacent resting site ahead, the interior remains negative; consequently, current flows internally from the excited depolarized site to the resting site ahead, not in the reverse direction. Hence, this direction of internal current flow is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding sodium inactivation and potassium activation
Sodium channel activation is brief and terminates rapidly as sodium channels inactivate, quickly followed by the opening of voltage-gated potassium channels that elevate potassium permeability to initiate repolarization. Hence, this temporal sequence is factually accurate.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements detailing sodium influx, polarity reversal, and subsequent potassium permeability rise are correct, whereas the statement claiming internal local current flows backward from resting to depolarized sites is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q06 - Chemical and electrical synaptic transmission mechanisms

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding impulse transmission across synapses:

Statement I: Impulse transmission across an electrical synapse is always faster than across a chemical synapse.

Statement II: At chemical synapses, arrival of an action potential stimulates synaptic vesicles to fuse with the pre-synaptic membrane and release neurotransmitters.

Statement III: Released neurotransmitters bind specifically to receptor molecules located on the pre-synaptic membrane to trigger post-synaptic depolarization.

Statement IV: Binding of neurotransmitters to specific receptors opens ion channels, which can develop either an excitatory or an inhibitory post-synaptic potential.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
Synapses transmit electrical signals between neurons either directly via electrical continuity across gap junctions or indirectly via chemical transmitters released into an intervening synaptic cleft.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding electrical synaptic conduction velocity
Electrical synapses transmit current directly across closely apposed membranes without the synaptic delays of transmitter exocytosis and diffusion, rendering transmission across an electrical synapse consistently faster than across a chemical synapse. Hence, this velocity comparison is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding pre-synaptic vesicle exocytosis
When an action potential arrives at the axon terminal of a chemical synapse, terminal depolarization induces synaptic vesicles to migrate toward and fuse with the pre-synaptic plasma membrane, discharging their neurotransmitter payload into the cleft. Hence, this exocytotic mechanism is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding receptor localization
Neurotransmitters diffuse across the synaptic cleft and bind specifically to receptor proteins located on the post-synaptic membrane; binding to pre-synaptic receptors does not mediate post-synaptic signal transduction. Hence, claiming that they bind to pre-synaptic receptors to induce post-synaptic responses is incorrect.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding post-synaptic potential polarity
The interaction between neurotransmitters and their post-synaptic receptors gates ion channels, permitting specific ionic movements that generate either a depolarizing excitatory post-synaptic potential or a hyperpolarizing inhibitory post-synaptic potential. Hence, this functional outcome is factually accurate.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements concerning electrical synapse speed, vesicle exocytosis, and post-synaptic potential generation are correct, while the statement mislocalizing receptor binding to the pre-synaptic membrane is incorrect.

answer.text: Statements I, II, and III are correct, while Statement IV is incorrect.
Statements I, II, and IV are correct, while Statement III is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q07 - Anatomy and functional organization of human forebrain

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the cranial meninges and the human forebrain:

Statement I: The cranial meninges protecting the brain comprise an outer dura mater, a thin middle arachnoid, and an inner pia mater that remains in direct contact with brain tissue.

Statement II: The left and right cerebral hemispheres are interconnected by a broad transverse tract of nerve fibres called the corpus callosum.

Statement III: The cerebral cortex contains association areas that are responsible for complex functions such as intersensory associations, memory, and communication.

Statement IV: The hypothalamus lies superior to the thalamus and acts primarily as an unintegrated relay centre lacking any endocrine or neurosecretory activity.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The human forebrain represents the principal region for executive cognition, sensory integration, and homeostatic neuroendocrine coordination, safeguarded externally by the trilaminar cranial meninges.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding cranial meningeal stratification
The cranial meninges consist of three membranes ordered from external to internal: the tough fibrous dura mater, the delicate web-like arachnoid, and the vascular pia mater adhering intimately to the cerebral convolutions. Hence, this anatomical layering is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding the corpus callosum
The two cerebral hemispheres are structurally and functionally linked across the longitudinal fissure by a massive commissural nerve tract designated the corpus callosum. Hence, this commissural description is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding cerebral association areas
The cerebral cortex contains prominent association areas that are neither purely sensory nor purely motor, serving integrative higher-order faculties including intersensory associations, memory storage, and communication. Hence, this functional assignment is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding hypothalamic anatomy and endocrinology
The hypothalamus lies at the base (inferior aspect) of the thalamus rather than superior to it, and it contains clusters of neurosecretory cells that synthesize hypothalamic hormones regulating the pituitary, alongside homeostatic centres for hunger, thirst, and body temperature. Hence, asserting that it lies superiorly and lacks neurosecretory activity is incorrect.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
Among the evaluated assertions, the statements describing the cranial meninges, the corpus callosum, and the cerebral association areas are correct, whereas the statement misrepresenting the position and neuroendocrine role of the hypothalamus is incorrect.

Statements II, III, and IV are correct, while Statement I is incorrect.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_STATEMENT_Q08 - Integrative structures of midbrain hindbrain brain stem

questiontext.text:
Consider the following four statements regarding the limbic system, midbrain, and hindbrain:

Statement I: The limbic system, formed by inner parts of cerebral hemispheres and associated deep structures like amygdala and hippocampus, interacts with the hypothalamus to regulate sexual behaviour and emotional reactions.

Statement II: The dorsal portion of the midbrain consists mainly of four round swellings called corpora quadrigemina, and a canal called the cerebral aqueduct passes through the midbrain.

Statement III: The cerebellum possesses a highly convoluted surface that provides additional space to accommodate large numbers of neurons.

Statement IV: The brain stem forms connections between the brain and spinal cord and is constituted by three major regions: the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata.

Choose the correct option from the following:

generalfeedback.text:
Step 1: Conceptual Principle
The subcortical limbic network orchestrates motivation and affective emotional responses, while the midbrain and hindbrain elements form the brain stem and coordinating centers regulating visceral survival reflexes and motor circuitry.

Step 2: Evaluation of the claim regarding the limbic system
The limbic system comprises deep structures including the hippocampus and amygdala along with the medial cerebral margin, acting in synergy with the hypothalamus to mediate emotional expressions such as fear, pleasure, and rage, as well as motivation and sexual behaviour. Hence, this functional anatomy is factually accurate.

Step 3: Evaluation of the claim regarding midbrain morphology
The midbrain contains a longitudinal conduit called the cerebral aqueduct and bears on its tectum (dorsal surface) four rounded collicular eminences collectively termed the corpora quadrigemina. Hence, this anatomical architecture is factually accurate.

Step 4: Evaluation of the claim regarding cerebellar surface convolutions
The cortex of the cerebellum exhibits extensive surface convolutions (folia) that substantially expand the available cortical surface area to house an enormous population of coordinating neurons. Hence, this structural feature is factually accurate.

Step 5: Evaluation of the claim regarding brain stem constituents
The brain stem forms the critical anatomical and functional axis between the brain and spinal cord and is specifically formed by three structures: the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata. Hence, this anatomical composition is factually accurate.

Step 6: Final Conclusion
All four evaluated assertions accurately describe the structural architecture and physiological roles of the limbic system, midbrain, cerebellum, and brain stem.
